resources.string:
"## Start here

This manual is bundled with Launcher and can be read offline. IRC and network services still need a connection. Read examples here; entering them at a live prompt can perform their described actions.

- IRC: open `irc`, connect to Libera.Chat or another network, join a channel, then talk. Several networks can be connected at once. Find IRC guides in Tools.
- Calculator: use 123, ABC and FUNC, check the interpretation/result hint, and use `to` for conversions. Read Calculator help in Tools.
- Floating tools: Calculator, Help and IRC start expanded, remember their window choice and retain their floating size. Find Floating tools in Appearance.
- Termux: the separate workspace has pages and up to two independent tiles. It offers a prompted update for the APK-bundled helper. Read Termux workspace and Helper updates in Automation.
- Presets: a shared .retui package is inspected and saved first, not immediately applied. Personal .retui-backup archives are separate. Read Portable preset import in Presets.
- Startup: new installs complete the introduction, configuration and build animation before entering Launcher. Existing completed setups are kept. Read Startup setup in Getting started.
- Appearance: app-drawer category/alphabet rails have independent normal and selected colors. The default font is JetBrains Mono Nerd Font Regular; custom/system font controls remain available.
- Idle fade: optionally fade Home and the Termux workspace to the wallpaper. It is off by default. Read Idle fade in Appearance.

## Recent updates

- Help home: use 10 from any article or topic list to return directly to the main directory.
- Notes: the library and editor share the terminal pane styling and background blur. Read Notes in Tools.
- Settings: swipe through Status, Terminal, Music, Help and Calculator previews before saving appearance changes. Read Configuration workflow in Appearance.
- Private Space: enable the private command in Behaviour on supported devices, unlock, then use `private -open <app name>`. Read Private Space in Apps.
- Calculator: basic arithmetic is ready immediately; advanced Qalculate is downloaded and installed after confirmation.

## Find an article directly

```
help -topic irc-community
```

At Launcher Home, open the offline IRC guide. `help irc` prints the shorter command reference instead. Use numbered choices or tap a topic in this reader; Android Back closes Help and keeps your place."

"## Open and connect

Enter `irc` at Launcher Home. The first time, Libera.Chat is selected. Tap Connect as … to join as a guest, or Sign in and enter your account name, then the masked password in the same composer. Change nickname picks the name others see.

Re:TUI's own IRC server has closed. Accounts and channels from it do not carry over; choose any public network instead.

Create account uses the same username/password flow on networks that allow signup from apps. On networks such as Libera.Chat, connect first, then use /register with your email address; the password is asked for separately and masked. Launcher never falls back to a guest connection when sign-in fails.

## Networks

The first chip under the conversation names the current network. Its marker counts unread messages and mentions on your other networks. Tap it for Networks: switch network, Add a network (Libera.Chat, OFTC, Rizon, hackint or any TLS server) or remove one. Every network stays connected while you switch.

Each network rejoins the channels you were in. Networks that were connected when you closed IRC reconnect when you open it again, when they need no password. A dropped connection retries by itself for a few minutes.

## Everyday navigation

1. Type a message in the active conversation and press ↵ to send.
2. Tap a named conversation chip to switch channels or private conversations. Unread counts and mention markers identify activity elsewhere.
3. Open Channels to switch to an open channel, browse the network, or join by name. Search text in navigation views is never posted as a message.

People lists nicknames in the active channel. Tap a nickname to open a private conversation; that alone sends nothing. Back first leaves a temporary view. From the conversation it closes the pane and disconnects every network.

## Optional slash commands

```
/network
/network add irc.oftc.net
/join #linux
/query nickname
/help
```

Use these inside IRC, not at Launcher Home. /network lists networks and switches; Alt+← and Alt+→ also switch. /join requests membership; /query opens a private conversation without sending. Typing / offers syntax hints. Unknown slash commands are rejected, never sent as messages. `//text` sends a literal leading slash.

## Sending safely

Messages appear immediately with their confirmation state. Server echo confirms server acceptance, not recipient delivery or a read receipt. Disconnect can leave a send uncertain; it is never automatically retried. Opening this offline article does not connect, join or send anything."

"## Remember this device

Remember this device asks the network's NickServ to trust a protected Android Keystore key after you sign in. Create account turns it on by default; you can turn it off. Passwords are not saved. Afterwards the network reconnects without a password and rejoins your channels. It works on networks whose services accept certificates, such as Libera.Chat and OFTC.

This is a device key, not a portable restore code. A new phone, reinstall, deleted app data or a missing key needs password sign-in again. Anyone using your unlocked Launcher can use the remembered account. Keep your account password recoverable independently.

## If reconnect fails

Check your network and the server, then use Reconnect or password Sign in. A rejected key or TLS failure never silently downgrades to a guest connection. Account names belong to one network; an account on one network is not an account on another.

## Forget this device

Connection details offers Forget this device. It deletes the key from this phone. The network may still list the certificate, but nothing can use it; remove it with NickServ CERT DEL from a signed-in client if you want. Removing a network also deletes its key. Neither deletes your account.

## Privacy and retention

TLS verifies and encrypts the connection, but messages are not end-to-end encrypted. Server operators can read channel and private messages and see your connection address. Each network has its own rules and history retention. Launcher keeps no transcript after you close IRC and has no background IRC service or push. Rotation retains conversations, but password entry cancels; leaving the pane disconnects."

"Calculator, Help and IRC start expanded. The header window control switches between expanded and floating. Drag a floating header to move the pane, or its corners to resize it within the safe screen area. Expanding preserves the floating rectangle for later. Each tool remembers its own mode and floating bounds when closed and reopened.

Calculator and Help stay expanded in landscape; IRC can still float. Calculator has a minimum size to keep its input, hint and keypad usable rather than shrinking the pad into a scrolling keyboard. Larger fonts or a smaller screen can require a larger minimum pane.

The tools follow Launcher fonts, colors and generated-border settings. Header controls and bottom-corner clearance keep resize targets distinct from editing keys. Changing border appearance does not change calculation or network behavior.

Help is a separate reader. Opening it from Calculator keeps the expression, answer and transcript intact. Android Back or 0 closes Help immediately; reopening resumes its saved article and reading position. Numbered Topics/Categories choices navigate inside Help instead of requiring repeated Back presses.

These are Launcher-owned tool windows, not Android split-screen controls. Floating does not create a background service or keep IRC connected after its pane closes."

"Idle fade is off by default. Enable breath_out in Settings and choose breath_out_seconds; its default timeout is 900 seconds (15 minutes). It fades Launcher Home and the dedicated Termux workspace to the wallpaper after inactivity. Calculator, Help and IRC are not additional fade targets.

The first touch, key or Back wakes a faded surface without performing the underlying action. Interact again to use that control. Typing restarts the timer. Backgrounding or loss of focus pauses active timing, and touch exploration prevents the fade. Disabling the feature restores the surface immediately.

This is visual fading, not screen locking, a security boundary, a phone-sleep command or a way to stop tmux jobs.

## Check the setting

```
config -get breath_out
config -get breath_out_seconds
```

These commands at Launcher Home only inspect the current values. To change them, use Settings or an explicit config -set. The two settings can be included in shareable presets."
"Update the Termux helper from the workspace"

"## Approve the matching helper

Opening the Termux workspace checks compatibility with the helper bundled in this APK. Update now installs that matching helper through Termux and reconnects the bridge. Later installs nothing. Inside the workspace, :update reopens the prompt. There is no silent update or background download from a changing Git branch.

The update replaces the normal helper path, including a custom helper there, only after approval. It verifies decoded bytes with SHA-256 and atomically replaces the file. Installation failures attempt rollback; the previous helper is retained at $PREFIX/share/retui/retui.previous. Existing shells, running jobs and workspace layout are kept. Only bridge connections restart.

## Setup is separate

Termux must already be installed, Launcher must have command permission, and allow-external-apps must be enabled in Termux by the user. If tmux or socat is missing, install them in Termux with pkg install tmux socat. The prompt offers permission, Termux and setup-guide actions; it does not silently grant access or install dependencies.

## If an update fails

Check the displayed error and prerequisites before retrying. A command with no reply may still finish inside Termux; Launcher does not automatically replay the installation. Leaving Launcher does not cancel a command already dispatched to Termux.

A lock prevents concurrent replacements. After an interrupted update, retry may report a running or interrupted lock. Launcher never deletes unknown locks automatically. Open the setup guide, inspect $PREFIX/share/retui/.update-lock only after checking that no updater is running, and retain the previous helper if recovery is needed. Never kill the tmux server as a routine update fix.

## Open the guide

```
help -topic termux-helper-updates
```

At Launcher Home, read this offline guide without changing the helper. :update belongs to the workspace local-control prompt, not the Home command parser."
